title: SKY & EARTH
blurb: Water, fire, soil, sun and rain.

radicals.name: WATER
radicals.origin: 水 is a stream with ripples on both sides. As a radical it shrinks to three drops on the left.
radicals.watch: Count the drops. Three is water 氵. Two is ice 冫, as in 冰 (ice) and 冷 (cold). And in 法 (fǎ, law) the water is only history.

radicals.name: FIRE
radicals.origin: 火 is a flame with two sparks. On the left it stays whole. Under a character it melts into four dots, 灬, like flames under a pot.
radicals.watch: Read a Chinese menu and you will meet this radical everywhere: 炒 stir-fried, 烤 roasted, 炸 deep-fried, 煮 boiled. Three dots standing on the left are water; four dots lying at the bottom are fire.

radicals.name: EARTH
radicals.origin: A mound of soil on the ground. On the left the bottom line tilts upward. At the bottom of a character it lies flat.
radicals.clue: soil, ground and things built from it
ex: cities had walls of packed earth
two people 人 on the ground
radicals.watch: Look-alike: 士 (scholar). In 土 the bottom line is the long one. In 士 the top line is longer.

radicals.name: SUN
radicals.origin: A circle with a dot in the middle, squared off over the centuries because brushes and chisels prefer straight lines.
radicals.watch: 日 also means day, so it shows up in time words: 时 (time), 昨 (yesterday), 星期日 (Sunday). Do not confuse it with 目 (eye), which has one more line inside.

radicals.name: RAIN
radicals.origin: Drops falling from a cloud under the sky. As a radical it flattens out and sits on top, like weather overhead.
radicals.clue: weather that comes from the sky
radicals.watch: 零 (líng, zero) first meant a light drizzle, then tiny leftovers, then nothing at all. Simplified Chinese also dropped the rain from 云 (cloud) and 电 (electricity, once lightning).
